extracted.intended_audience: industry petitioners, ANDA/505(b)(2)/351(k) applicants, regulatory counsel, and commenters submitting or responding to citizen petitions or petitions for stay under FDA section 505(q)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and evaluating citizen petitions and petitions for stay of action that may be subject to section 505(q) of the FD&C Act, including applicability, timelines, certification/verification requirements, and factors for denial. It also explains the relationship between petition review and pending ANDA/505(b)(2)/351(k) application review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of section 505(q)
rubrics_metrics.description: We interpret section 505(q) to apply to a petition only if the petition meets all of the following: (1) submitted on or after Sept 27, 2007 (for ANDA/505(b)(2) subject matter) or on or after July 9, 2012 (for 351(k) subject matter); (2) submitted in writing and pursuant to 21 CFR 10.30 or 10.35; (3) an ANDA, 505(b)(2), or 351(k) application related to the subject matter is pending at the time the petition is submitted and at least one such application’s user fee goal date is on or before the 150-day deadline for final Agency action on the petition; (4) the petitioner requests an action that could delay approval of a pending ANDA/505(b)(2)/351(k); and (5) the petition does not fall within any of the exceptions described in section 505(q)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance explains each element in detail (see separate metrics). FDA evaluates these elements at the time of submission (no rolling evaluation). If any element is not met, FDA will not consider section 505(q) to apply, though FDA will still review and respond to petitions under regular regulations in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission date thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q) applies only to petitions submitted on or after Sept 27, 2007 for issues related to ANDAs or 505(b)(2) applications, and on or after July 9, 2012 for issues related to 351(k) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions submitted before these dates generally are not subject to 505(q) (and would also lack the statutory certification). If submitted before the effective date, the statute is not interpreted to apply retroactively; applying it retroactively could impose statutory-day deadlines that already passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submission pursuant to 21 CFR 10.30 or 10.35
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 505(q), a petition must be submitted in writing and pursuant to § 10.30 (citizen petition) or § 10.35 (request for administrative stay of action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications with potential to delay approval should be submitted via the petition process (§10.30/§10.35), not as correspondence to the application (NDA/ANDA/505(b)(2)/351(a)/351(k)). Petitioners may not cross-reference or rely on information not included in the petition; information referred to must be included in full or previously submitted in the same proceeding (21 CFR 10.20(c)). Comments on petitions should be filed in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related pending application and user fee goal date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q) applies only if, at the time the petition is submitted, at least one related ANDA, 505(b)(2), or 351(k) application is pending and at least one such application's user fee goal date is on or before the 150-day deadline for final Agency action on the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA evaluates 'pending' and user fee goal dates at time of submission; if no related application is pending or the applicable goal date falls after the petition's 150-day period, 505(q) does not apply. This aligns petition timelines with application review commitments and avoids a 'rolling' evaluation that could change petition status mid-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested action must be capable of delaying approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q) is implemented only for petitions that request an action that could delay approval of a pending ANDA, 505(b)(2) application, or 351(k) application. If the action requested does not have the potential to delay approval under any reasonable theory, 505(q) does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will assess whether the petition's requested action could reasonably cause a delay; purely policy or general standards petitions may be treated differently from those that raise narrow approvability issues for a specific pending application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to coverage under section 505(q)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q)(4) provides that 505(q) will not apply to petitions that: (a) relate solely to the timing of approval pursuant to the 180-day exclusivity under 505(j)(5)(B)(iv); or (b) are from the applicant of the ANDA, 505(b)(2), or 351(k) application and seek only to have FDA take or refrain from taking action with respect to that applicant's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either exception applies, FDA will not apply the 505(q) provisions to the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 150-day deadline for final Agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 505(q)(1)(F), FDA shall take final Agency action on a petition not later than 150 days after the date on which the petition is submitted. The 150-day period is not to be extended for any reason (including determinations, supplements, or petitioner consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions submitted between Sept 27, 2007 and July 9, 2012 may be subject to the prior 180-day deadline; FDA treats the 150-day timeline as strict for qualifying petitions and will not extend it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for petitions submitted primarily to delay (section 505(q)(1)(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may deny a petition or supplement at any point if it determines the petition was submitted with the primary purpose of delaying approval of an application and the petition does not on its face raise valid scientific or regulatory issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may summarily deny such petitions; it may also issue guidance (this document) describing factors to determine whether a petition's primary purpose is delay. If determined, FDA may note that determination in its response, refer matters to the FTC, and summarize such findings in reports to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to applicant when delay is necessary to protect public health
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines a delay of approval is necessary to protect the public health, FDA must provide the applicant, not later than 30 days after making the determination: (1) Notification that the determination has been made; (2) if applicable, any clarification or additional data the applicant should submit to the petition docket to allow prompt review; and (3) a brief summary of the specific substantive issues raised in the petition which form the basis of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may convey this information by document or meeting. Information conveyed is part of the application and subject to disclosure requirements. FDA does not intend to notify the petitioner of such a determination (statute does not require notification).

rubrics_metrics.name: But-for test for whether a petition would delay approval
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA uses a but-for test: would the ANDA, 505(b)(2), or 351(k) application be ready for approval but for the issues raised by the petition? If the application would not be ready for approval regardless (e.g., applicant receives a complete response letter during the 150-day period), the petition would not delay approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application would be ready but for resolution of petition issues within the 150-day period, FDA next determines whether a delay is necessary to protect the public health (see related metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether delay is necessary to protect the public health
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA determines necessity of delay based on preliminary evaluation: if approval occurred before substantive review of the petition and, after further review, FDA concluded the petitioner's arguments against approval were meritorious, could the presence on the market of products not meeting requirements identified by the petitioner negatively affect public health?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of issues implicating public health include bioequivalence concerns and whether an indication can be safely omitted because it is patent-protected. If FDA concludes a public health risk exists, it will delay approval until issues are resolved, then notify applicant per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement (section 505(q)(1)(H))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q)(1)(H) provides that FDA shall not consider a petition for review unless the petition is in writing and signed and contains the statutory certification (verbatim text provided in statute). The certification includes: (a) the petition includes all information and views upon which it relies; (b) it includes representative data/information unfavorable to the petition; (c) petitioner took reasonable steps to ensure unfavorable information was disclosed; (d) the date on or about which the information first became known to the party; (e) disclosure of payments or consideration received or expected to be received to file the information; and (f) verification under penalty of perjury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 21 CFR 10.31 also requires the certification for certain petitions; certification is required for every petition requesting any action that could delay approval, regardless of whether petition is ultimately subject to the statutory deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification completeness and verbatim requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will evaluate whether the language of the petition's certification exactly mirrors the language provided in section 505(q) and whether the petitioner provided a month, day, and year date for when the information first became known to the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification is deficient if every word in the petitioner's certification does not match every word of the statutory certification (verbatim). The date must include month, day, and year (e.g., 'May 2010' alone is deficient). The blank space may accommodate explanatory information or multiple dates tied to specific information, but inserted explanatory text must not alter the statutory words outside the blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification cannot be cured by supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the statute requires the certification in the petition, FDA would not be able to review a petition submitted before the applicable effective date if it lacks the required certification, and the statute does not permit a petitioner to cure the deficiency by supplementing the petition to add the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 505(q) applies but the petition is not in writing or signed, or does not contain the complete certification, FDA will not review the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification requirement for supplemental information/comments (section 505(q)(1)(I))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA shall not accept for review any supplemental information or comments on a petition unless the submission is in writing, signed, and contains the statutory verification: includes certification that the submitter has not intentionally delayed submission, the date on or about which the information first became known to the submitter (month/day/year), disclosure of payments received or expected, and verification under penalty of perjury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 21 CFR 10.31 contains a minor technical correction (uses 'document' instead of statutory 'petition'); FDA will accept either 'petition' or 'document' in the final sentence. A verification that does not exactly mirror the required text or lacks the full date is deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deficient verification or supplemental submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not review supplemental information or comments on petitions subject to 505(q) if the supplemental information or comments are missing the required verification or contain an incomplete verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petitioner/commenter submitted supplemental information without the required verification or with an incomplete verification and wants FDA review, they should resubmit the supplemental information or comments with the required verification. Petitioners/commenters should not rely on FDA to notify them that their supplements will not be reviewed; in some dockets it is administratively burdensome to monitor and notify commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between petition review and application review; limits on substantive action
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition responses constitute final Agency action and are subject to judicial review; by contrast, application review is governed by statutory/regulatory procedures that provide procedural protections for applicants. FDA does not interpret 505(q) to require substantive final Agency decisions within 150 days on the approvability of a specific aspect of a pending application when such decisions could deprive applicants of procedural rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a petition requests action related to a specific aspect of a pending application and rendering a substantive decision would interfere with the established application review process and rights, FDA would typically deny the petition without substantive comment. FDA may respond to general policy or standards petitions without commenting on approvability of specific pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and final Agency action timing (section 505(q)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is considered to have taken final Agency action on a petition if FDA makes a final decision under 21 CFR 10.45(d) during the 150-day period or the 150-day period expires without FDA making a final decision. If a civil action is filed before final Agency action, a court shall dismiss the action without prejudice for failure to exhaust administrative remedies. Section 505(q)(2)(C) describes information to include in the administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial review provisions do not apply to petitions addressing issues concerning a 351(k) application (section 505(q)(2) exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations that may indicate a petition was submitted primarily to delay approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors FDA expects to consider (not exhaustive and no single factor determinative) include: submission long after relevant information became known; submission of multiple/serial petitions or supplements raising issues that could have been known earlier; submission close in time to a known possible approval date (e.g., end of exclusivity or patent-related timing); submission with little or no supporting data; raising same/substantially similar issues as a prior petition recently responded to by FDA; submitting petitions on standards for approval where FDA already sought public input but petitioner did not use that process; requesting other applicants meet standards more onerous than FDA has determined are necessary; and the petitioner's history with FDA (e.g., history of delay-oriented petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FDA determines a petition's primary purpose is delay, it may summarily deny the petition if it does not on its face raise valid scientific/regulatory issues, may refer matters to the FTC, and will highlight such determinations in the annual report to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include all information the petition relies upon (including unfavorable data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must include all information and views upon which the petition relies and representative data/information known to the petitioner which are unfavorable to the petition (part of the statutory certification). Under 21 CFR 10.20(c), information referred to or relied upon must be included in full and may not be incorporated by reference unless previously submitted in the same proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should contain both favorable and unfavorable information regarding the petitioner's claims; failure to include relied-upon information risks non-consideration under 505(q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing of communications and docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications about issues with potential to delay approval should be submitted through the petition process (§10.30/§10.35) and not as correspondence to the application; citizen petition comments should be filed in the appropriate docket and not to the NDA/ANDA/505(b)(2)/351(a) BLA/351(k) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA provides examples (e.g., bioequivalence views should be submitted in response to Federal Register notices on product-specific recommendations rather than as a petition) and notes that the petition process is the appropriate channel for such issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative evaluation at time of submission (no rolling status)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will determine whether a related application is pending and whether 505(q) applies at the time the petition is submitted, not on a rolling basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rolling approach could change petition status mid-review and disrupt orderly implementation; evaluating at submission prevents prejudice to petitioners/commenters and procedural disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and confidentiality constraints on responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Information conveyed as part of the notification to an applicant (when FDA determines delay is necessary) is to be considered part of the application and subject to disclosure requirements applicable to information in applications. FDA is generally prohibited from disclosing information regarding applications that have not yet been approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations on disclosure may circumscribe FDA's ability to respond substantively to petitions that affect pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time to prepare the information collections: 30 minutes to prepare a certification under section 505(q)(1)(H) for citizen petitions and petitions for stay; 30 minutes to prepare a verification under section 505(q)(1)(I) for supplements/comments; and 30 minutes to prepare a letter withdrawing a deficient petition for stay of action missing the required certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates include review of instructions, searching data sources, gathering data, and completing/reviewing the information collection. OMB control numbers and related regulatory information are cited.
